title: PeMS Data Quality
text:
2025 PeMS 5-Minute Interval Data

Before station-days are even assembled, individual five-minute records are dropped when they fail basic sanity checks (missing timestamp/station, non-positive sample counts, or missing traffic-flow values). This section measures that upstream loss directly, out of 25,297,920 raw records ingested.









The two dominant conditions above, invalid sample counts and missing flow values, overlap: a record can fail both at once. The chart below shows how much each filter catches independently versus together.









508 of 1,440 stations (35.3%) have zero surviving records after filtering — they are entirely absent from every downstream table.
Beyond whether a record is valid, percent_observed measures how much of each five-minute reading is actual sensor data versus imputed/estimated. The chart below buckets every raw record (valid or not) by this value. No filter on percent_observed was adopted as previous filters already addressed most cases (see below).

title: PeMS Data Quality
text:
Completeness by Time Period
The chart below shows the number of station-days that do not contain the expected number of five-minute observations in each model time period. These are dropped in gold layer.









Incompleteness isn’t all-or-nothing: the chart below buckets every station-day by what share of its 288 expected five-minute intervals were actually present. Only -87.2% were dropped in this process.









Over that same population, the chart below buckets station-days by their average percent_observed — “100” means fully observed all day with no imputation; lower buckets rely on increasing amounts of estimated values.
